top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P002) is my first choice on the common criteria. His voice is distinctive: in the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid, body, childhood memory, dream and metaphysical speculation form one imaginative system in dense, patterned prose. The formal ambition is sustained across large cycles rather than isolated books. Recasting a visionary and modernist inheritance as a personal cosmology shows imaginative and intellectual depth. The oeuvre spans decades and moves between intimate and cosmic registers. I would centre the citation on the novels, with the poetry as foundation, because coverage of the poetry in translation is thin. Can Xue (P001) is a very close second. I find her formal rigour and compression persuasive, and the choice between the two is narrow and could reasonably go the other way. The main open question for both is whether recurrence is structural or thinning, and I cannot settle it for either from the supplied evidence. My judgment rests on public knowledge and translation, and I have not independently verified any text. Both writers are far preferable to no award (P000), which I rank last because two serious single-writer proposals are available.
